question: whats the actual difference between a virus and bacteria?? like why wont the doctor give me antibiotics for a cold
expected: Bacteria are single-celled living organisms that can reproduce on their own; viruses are much smaller, not cells, and can only replicate inside a host's cells. Antibiotics target bacterial structures/processes (cell walls, bacterial ribosomes), so they do nothing against cold viruses; prescribing them for a cold adds side effects and drives antibiotic resistance. Colds are treated with rest, fluids and symptom relief; seeing a provider (e.g., Ramapo Health Services) makes sense if symptoms are severe or last a long time.

note: Pure general knowledge; a Ramapo pointer is optional.
